transcript:
Header: 2027-09-08 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Solara), Mark Li (Solara), Asha Raman (Solara)

Summary: quick integration discovery for Solara Fintech evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Focus: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy architecture, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Action items and next steps captured at end.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, uh we've got Diego from our solutions engineering team as well. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya: good thanks, yeah excited to, to dig in.
[00:08] Mark: hi all, thanks for making time.
[00:11] Diego: great, quick agenda: integration patterns, SDKs & community adapter support (LangChain / LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy setup for traffic, rate limit behaviour and quota, and observability hooks (traces, token-level costs). then Q&A. sound good?
[00:20] Priya: yep perfect.
[00:22] Diego: to start can you share a bit about your stack and what you're trying to build?
[00:27] Priya: sure, we're building an AI assistant for merchant support and risk scoring for transactions. primary infra is k8s on GCP, some services in AWS. latency targets are pretty tight for chat flows, 150-200ms tail ideally. throughput varies — spikes up to 400 QPS during peak, typical baseline 80 QPS. we care about PII handling and audit trails.
[00:46] Mark: we currently evaluate a mix of OpenAI for experiments, but for production we want more control and cost predictability. interested in Redwood because of Dedicated / Private options.
[00:56] Diego: got it, thanks. on the integration side we expose a simple REST API and SDKs for node/python, plus official adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex. do you use either today?
[01:07] Priya: our platform team has LangChain in a couple of services — mainly orchestrating prompts across chains. LlamaIndex is used by the docs search team.
[01:14] Diego: perfect — we have example notebooks that show Redwood client wrapped as a LangChain llm wrapper and a LlamaIndex connector. small caveat: depending on the model and quantization you pick, the streaming semantics are slightly different — but we provide the same streaming hooks across hosted and dedicated.
[01:29] Asha: quick question on private deployments — if we go VPC/private, does the SDK change? and what about internal gateway?
[01:36] Maya: good q. SDK surface is the same, the only difference is endpoint URL and auth: hosted calls our public endpoint, dedicated gets a customer-specific subdomain with creds, private is behind your VPC with a private control plane. Diego, want to add on gateway?
[01:47] Diego: yeah so most customers deploy a small gateway/proxy in front of Redwood endpoints for routing, canarying, and auth. typical pattern: envoy or nginx in k8s that forwards to Redwood Dedicated, or for Private you point the gateway to the private endpoint. the gateway also enforces rate limits and request validation.
[02:05] Mark: does Redwood offer a managed gateway?
[02:08] Maya: we have a recommended reference gateway config and a lightweight proxy we can share, but we don't mandate customers run our gateway — many run their own. for Dedicated we offer optional managed ingress for an extra fee.
[02:19] Priya: on rate limits — how are quotas handled across teams? we have multiple internal tenants.
[02:24] Diego: quotas are per API key by default; for Dedicated we can map to per-route or per-team quotas and integrate with your SSO to map roles. Hosted gives usage quotas and org-level rate limits, Dedicated adds more granularity and private includes full RBAC.
[02:39] Asha: and billing granularity — token-level cost? how easy to attribute costs to teams?
[02:44] Maya: Console shows token-level breakdowns per API key and route, plus per-model cost. for Dedicated you can export usage logs or integrate with our tracing hooks to bring into your cost pipeline.
[02:56] Mark: you mentioned observability hooks — what telemetry do you expose?
[03:00] Diego: we emit request traces with trace IDs, token counts, model id, latency buckets and optional embeddings metrics. integrations: Datadog/Prometheus exporters, and you can push traces to your tracing backend. we also support structured logs and a webhook for important events.
[03:16] Priya: are logs PII-safe? can we strip prompt bodies before sending out?
[03:20] Diego: yes, you control what we store. for hosted we default to ephemeral storage but can enable no-persist mode; for Dedicated/Private data never leaves your VPC and we support KMS/HSM for keys. we'll share the security whitepaper.
[03:33] Asha: about SDKs — do you have typed clients? Typescript/types?
[03:37] Diego: node/python both have typed clients; TS client ships with types for responses and streaming events. we also have example LangChain chain wrappers and LlamaIndex connectors in our repo.
[03:46] Mark: if we use LangChain, do we need to change prompts or config for the batching that Redwood does?
[03:51] Diego: batching is mostly server-side and handled by the runtime. for lower latency you can disable batching per-route; we also recommend pinning model variants. with LangChain you can use our callback handlers to surface streaming tokens.
[04:04] Priya: about network topology: we have services in both AWS and GCP, is cross-cloud private deployment supported?
[04:11] Maya: Private deployments are flexible — we can do VPC peering or on-prem package. Dedicated can be provisioned in a chosen cloud region. we'll need to look at your network layout for egress.
[04:22] Mark: security/compliance question — SOC2 / ISO?
[04:25] Maya: we are SOC2 Type II and have ISO docs; we'll send the packet. also support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, audit logs.
[04:34] Asha: do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:36] Diego: yes, KMS integration and HSM for private deployments.
[04:40] Priya: pricing — rough ballpark for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:44] Maya: high-level: hosted is pay-as-you-go per token with tiered discounts at volume. Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity with monthly commit; pricing depends on capacity and SLA. Private adds a platform fee. we'll send specific numbers in follow-up.
[04:57] Mark: ok great. one more technical: can we run custom model artifacts or only models in your catalog?
[05:03] Diego: Dedicated and Private support customer-uploaded model artifacts if they meet runtime constraints — e.g., supported architecture and quantization. hosted is restricted to our catalog for security.
[05:13] Priya: about quota enforcement during peaks — if we hit burst above our committed, what's the fallback?
[05:18] Diego: for Dedicated we support burst capacity options and automated fallback to compatible hosted model variants if configured. for strict isolation customers can disable fallback.
[05:28] Asha: observability again — can we push token-level traces into our APM?
[05:31] Diego: yes, via our tracing exporter; we include token counts and model selection metadata.
[05:38] Priya: what's the onboarding time for Dedicated vs Private?
[05:41] Maya: Dedicated typically 2-6 weeks depending on capacity; Private (VPC/on-prem) can range 6-12 weeks based on networking and compliance.
[05:50] Mark: are there SDK examples for error handling and retry semantics?
[05:54] Diego: yes, clients include recommended retry policies, idempotency keys for non-streaming requests, and examples for streaming reconnect.
[06:03] Priya: ok let's talk about immediate pilot: we want a small POC with 10 QPS steady and some spike tests. can Redwood run a benchmark?
[06:11] Maya: yes, we can run a benchmark from our side or you can run locally with our sample harness. Diego will prepare a benchmark guide and a LangChain notebook.
[06:20] Mark: timeline: if we get security docs next week and run a benchmark week after, we can decide by end of month.
[06:27] Maya: sounds good — next steps: we'll send security pack, benchmark guide, LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repo, and pricing options for Hosted/Dedicated. can you share sample prompts and expected QPS?
[06:38] Priya: yes we'll share a prompt set and team QPS.
[06:41] Asha: one last question — do you support model explainability hooks or provenance metadata?
[06:46] Diego: we emit model/version metadata per response and token-level attribution hooks in our structured output if you enable eval tracing. not full explainability but metadata to tie responses back to prompt versions.
[06:59] Maya: great, we're at 48 minutes — thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the docs and Diego will send the LangChain examples.
[07:07] Priya: thanks all.

Recap / Next steps:
- Maya to send security whitepaper + SOC2 and pricing (due 2027-09-10)
- Diego to prepare LangChain/LlamaIndex sample notebook and benchmark guide (due 2027-09-13)
- Solara to share prompt sets and traffic profile (due 2027-09-10)
- Schedule benchmark run / demo next week (owner: Mark)

References mentioned: "Redwood SDK repo" (link shared in chat), LangChain adapters, LlamaIndex connector, reference gateway config (envoy/nginx), security whitepaper.

End of transcript.
